catalog.name: Openterface Mini-KVM Toolkit
catalog.description: Use a laptop as a local console for a headless computer.
verificationNotes: Primary-source claims checked independently; no hands-on testing or maker relationship. Price and checkout stock remain unverified.
Exact toolkit SKU 392-OPMINIKVMTOOLKIT; hardware revision is not guaranteed by this bundle identifier. USB switching from software requires v1.9+.

usage.goodFor: Configure or recover a nearby headless computer.
usage.needs: A host with the Openterface app and a powered target with HDMI output and USB control.
usage.tradeoff: 1080p30 capture; older BIOS USB-hub compatibility varies.

rows.label: Selection
rows.value: Toolkit 392-OPMINIKVMTOOLKIT; Basic is a different bundle.

rows.label: In the bag
rows.value: Mini-KVM, quickstart, carry bag and extension-pin cap.

rows.label: Video cable
rows.value: 0.3 m HDMI male-to-male.

rows.label: USB cables
rows.value: 0.3 m C-to-A with A-female/C-male adapter; 1.5 m C-to-C with C-female/A-male adapter.

rows.label: Size
rows.value: 61 × 13.5 × 53 mm; 48 g for the device.

rows.label: Host side
rows.value: Orange USB-C side → host with the 1.5 m cable; install Openterface first.

rows.label: Target side
rows.value: Black USB-C → target USB; target video → HDMI input. Target needs no Openterface app.

rows.label: Video limit
rows.value: Up to 3840 × 2160 at 30 Hz input; capture up to 1920 × 1080 at 30 Hz.

rows.label: Audio
rows.value: Captures embedded HDMI audio.

rows.label: Power
rows.value: USB power can come from either side. Use a dedicated supply for low-power targets such as Raspberry Pi.

rows.label: Optional USB devices
rows.value: Connection guide limits peripherals to 1.5 W and recommends externally powered hubs.

rows.label: File transfer
rows.value: The switchable USB-A port moves an attached drive between host and target.

rows.label: Revision-specific control
rows.value: USB-port switching through software needs hardware v1.9 or newer.

rows.label: Practical limit
rows.value: Some older BIOS implementations do not recognize the internal USB hub.

rows.label: Host downloads
rows.value: Official apps for macOS, Windows, Linux and Android; select the host platform on the download page.

rows.label: Firmware troubleshooting
rows.value: The FAQ directs capture-firmware recovery to the QT releases. Follow the matching release instructions.

rows.label: Hardware source
rows.value: Schematics/design repository uses CERN-OHL-S-2.0; its documentation is declared CC BY-SA 4.0.

rows.label: Useful outcome
rows.value: A nearby laptop can provide the console for a headless SBC or mini-PC without a network KVM.

gaps: The datasheet calls port ② a host connection; the dedicated connection guide identifies it as target keyboard/mouse output. This profile follows the connection guide.
The toolkit SKU does not establish the shipped PCB revision or capture firmware. Record both before publishing a tested setup.
The site navigation advertises an iPadOS app, while the dedicated app page lists four other platforms. iPad host requirements remain unverified here.
No exact recovery binary, universal BIOS compatibility, measured latency or adapter compatibility was tested.
Repository documentation has a stated CC BY-SA license; the scope of any selected product photo still needs an asset-level record. The media index includes third-party content.
Price, regional fulfillment and current checkout stock remain unverified.
notes: Independently checked against primary sources; no hands-on testing. Listed status does not guarantee stock, fulfillment, performance or accessory compatibility.

rows.label: Selected package
rows.value: Cynthion board in its CNC-milled anodized-aluminum enclosure; bare-board listing is separate.

rows.label: Confirmed release
rows.value: r1.4.0 is labeled the initial production hardware release.

rows.label: Check your unit
rows.value: Connect CONTROL and run cynthion info --force-offline to read hardware and firmware information.

rows.label: Core hardware
rows.value: Lattice LFE5U-12F ECP5 FPGA; Microchip SAMD11 debug controller.

rows.label: Memory
rows.value: 8 MiB RAM and 4 MiB SPI flash.

rows.label: USB interfaces
rows.value: Three USB3343 PHYs, each supporting up to 480 Mbit/s.

rows.label: Expansion
rows.value: Two Pmod-compatible connectors expose 16 FPGA I/O signals.

rows.label: Scope
rows.value: Cynthion hardware does not support SuperSpeed; LUNA gateware is a separate project.

rows.label: Cables
rows.value: Maker's shipping update says USB cables are not included; choose cables for your host and target ports.

rows.label: Host software
rows.value: Python 3.9+ and the cynthion package; Linux needs access rules and macOS needs native libusb.

rows.label: Packetry
rows.value: Documented installers: Linux AppImage, macOS Homebrew and Windows installer; source builds are also documented.

rows.label: Analyzer firmware
rows.value: Factory FPGA configuration is USB Analyzer. cynthion run analyzer loads it; cynthion flash analyzer makes it the default.

rows.label: Update path
rows.value: cynthion update updates MCU firmware and FPGA flash; record installed versions first.

rows.label: Analysis connection
rows.value: CONTROL → computer running Packetry; TARGET C → target host; TARGET A → device under test.

rows.label: One computer
rows.value: The tutorial permits one host for both roles, with CONTROL and TARGET C on different hubs.

rows.label: Capture sequence
rows.value: Start capture before attaching the target to include enumeration. Match the target speed if the UI requests it.

rows.label: Documented result
rows.value: The keyboard tutorial inspects enumeration plus key press/release transfers.

rows.label: Device supply
rows.value: 5 V DC for Cynthion itself. Use USB cables no longer than 2 m.

rows.label: Target supply
rows.value: Pass-through supply: 5–20 V, up to 3 A; target must match voltage/current. Cynthion-supplied target load: at most 500 mA.

rows.label: Expansion voltage
rows.value: Pmod and mezzanine connectors must not exceed 3.3 V.

rows.label: Other modes
rows.value: Facedancer and LUNA provide USB-device development paths beyond Packetry analysis.

rows.label: Design downloads
rows.value: r1.4.0 archive includes schematics, assembly diagrams, BOM, placement and Gerber files.

rows.label: Hardware license
rows.value: The hardware design repository uses CERN-OHL-P-2.0.

gaps: r1.4.0 is a confirmed production design release. The reviewed store does not guarantee a shipping revision; inspect the actual unit before selecting revision-specific files.
One-host capture depends on USB topology. No target, operating system, hub or USB-C cable combination was physically tested.
The keyboard tutorial uses manual speed selection while newer Packetry instructions omit that step; follow the installed version's UI.
Factory firmware version, present distributor cable bundles, current price and checkout stock remain unverified.
The hardware license does not establish permission for the storefront photo. Any published asset needs its own source, rights and attribution record.
notes: Independently checked against primary sources; no hands-on testing. Listed status does not guarantee stock, fulfillment, performance or accessory compatibility.

rows.label: Model
rows.value: Beryl AX GL-MT3000.

rows.label: Processor and memory
rows.value: MT7981B dual-core 1.3 GHz; 512 MB DDR4; 256 MB NAND flash.

rows.label: Wi-Fi
rows.value: 2.4 / 5 GHz 802.11ax; two retractable antennas.

rows.label: Ethernet
rows.value: One 2.5 Gb/s WAN port and one 1 Gb/s LAN port.

rows.label: USB
rows.value: One USB 3.0 peripheral port; USB-C is the specified power input.

rows.label: Power
rows.value: USB-C 5 V / 3 A; maker lists consumption below 8 W.

rows.label: In the package
rows.value: Router, Ethernet cable, power adapter and country-dependent converter, plus printed documents.

rows.label: First connection
rows.value: Power on; join its labeled Wi-Fi network or connect to LAN by Ethernet.

rows.label: Administration
rows.value: Open 192.168.8.1 in a browser and set an admin password.

rows.label: Uplink choices
rows.value: Ethernet WAN, Wi-Fi repeater, USB phone tethering or a cellular USB modem.

rows.label: Phone tethering
rows.value: Use a USB data cable, enable tethering on the phone, then connect from the router's Tethering panel.

rows.label: Cellular prerequisite
rows.value: Cellular mode needs an external USB modem.

rows.label: Documented outcome
rows.value: A repeater connection can provide Wi-Fi for several devices through an upstream hotspot.

rows.label: Portal behavior
rows.value: Login Mode is documented for firmware 4.6+; it temporarily suspends some services and switches DNS to automatic.

rows.label: Firmware family
rows.value: Maker supplies OpenWrt-based firmware and links a GL-MT3000-specific download selector.

rows.label: VPN options
rows.value: Model guide documents OpenVPN and WireGuard client/server setup.

rows.label: WireGuard prerequisites
rows.value: Use a provider's credentials or configuration file; the current guide targets firmware 4.7+ with an older-version selector.

gaps: Exact shipping-country plug, regional stock, checkout price and supplied firmware version remain unverified.
The firmware selector requires a dynamic interface; no current stable binary/version was verified. Vendor firmware and upstream OpenWrt are separate installation paths.
Package list names a power adapter and converter but does not separately itemize a detachable USB power cable. Do not promise an extra cable.
External modem/phone compatibility, captive-portal operation, Wi-Fi range, VPN throughput and power-bank operation require setup-specific testing.
Firmware menus differ across releases. Portal login can suspend services; do not imply that VPN protection remains active throughout authentication.

The product links a media kit, but readable asset-specific terms were unavailable. Website terms require permission for commercial content reuse; obtain a precise grant before using product photography.
notes: Independently checked against primary sources; no hands-on testing. Listed status does not guarantee stock, fulfillment, performance or accessory compatibility.
